prompt:
In the 1930s, librarian Pura Belpré began telling stories in Spanish and English at New York Public Library branches. At a time when many library programs offered few materials for Puerto Rican children, Belpré’s storytelling helped make the library feel more ______ to families who had recently moved to the city.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
explanation: The text says Belpré’s storytelling helped families feel included in the library, so “welcoming” is the most precise choice.

prompt:
Some rivers carry dark-colored water because leaves and other plant materials release natural compounds as they decay. These “blackwater” rivers may look muddy, but many are actually low in sediment. Their color comes mostly from dissolved organic matter rather than from soil particles.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Blackwater rivers can appear muddy even though their dark color often comes from dissolved plant material.
choices.B: Blackwater rivers are always more polluted than clear rivers.
choices.C: Soil particles are the only reason river water can look dark.
choices.D: Decaying leaves prevent rivers from supporting plant and animal life.

explanation: The passage explains that blackwater rivers may look muddy but usually get their color from dissolved organic matter.

prompt:

prompt:

choices.D: It gives instructions for drawing sea monsters accurately.

explanation: The quoted sentence explains that the drawings often marked danger or unfamiliar places rather than actual sightings.

prompt:

prompt:

choices.D: It helps them find warmer places to sleep.
